parole.significato: tusk, fang (e.g. that of an elephant or a boar)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *ɨnćara, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ońćarɜ (“tusk”). Doublet of acsarkodik.
From Proto-Ugric *påda, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *padɜ. Cognates include Finnish pato (“dam”).
From Proto-Ugric *pekkɜ- (“to split, crack, tear”) + -ly. A possible front-vowel variant of Proto-Finno-Ugric *pakka- (“to tear, split, rend”). Compare Hungarian fakad and fakaszt.

parole.significato: to sharpen, to whet, to hone

parole.testo: Probably from Proto-Ugric *puśɜ- (“rag; to dissolve, fray”) (perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric?) + -lik (“verb-forming suffix”).
First attested in c. 1395. Probably from Proto-Ugric *puśɜ- (“rag; to dissolve, fray”) (perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric?) + -t (causative suffix).

parole.significato: to lace (to fasten a shoe with laces)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *pĭtä-, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *pitɜ- (“to bind, to fasten, to tie up”). Related to Eastern Mari пидаш (pidaš, “to tie, to bind, to knit”).

parole.significato: come and go, get about (to transport oneself from place to place)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric *kälä-, possibly derived from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kälä- (“to ford”). Akin to Northern Mansi ква̄луӈкве (kvāluňkve, “to rise”).
Probably from Proto-Ugric. Another source indicates Proto-Finno-Ugric *kitɜ (“middle, gap”). Related to Eastern Khanty кӱтәп (kütəp, “middle, center; waist”).

parole.significato: to fight (whether literally or figuratively; for something: -ért or against something: ellen; (optionally) with someone…
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric or perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric *kᴕ̈śɜ (“competition, game; to compete, play”) + -d (frequentative suffix).
A word with disputed origins: # From Proto-Ugric *ńolɜ- (“to press”). # From Proto-Finno-Ugric *ńȣmɜ- (“to press, compress, crush”).

From a root of uncertain origin, perhaps Proto-Ugric or Proto-Finno-Ugric + -g (nominal suffix). The sz must have been a frequentative suffix that became part of the word. Its meaning may have referred to the saman's trance. (In the 1830s, Gregor Dankovszky compared the term to Austrian and Zipser G

parole.significato: part, phase, stage, section (e.g. of a day or a year)
parole.testo: From Proto-Ugric or perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric.
From *tätwə, from Proto-Ugric *täjəktəm (cf. Northern Mansi та̄кум (tākum), Northern Khanty тевтәм (tjewtəm)), from Proto-Finno-Ugric *täje (“louse”). Cognates include Finnish täi.

From Proto-Ugric *waŋke- (“to strike, cut”) or perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric *waŋɜ (“to strike, cut”). Cognates include Udmurt вандыны (vandyny, “to cut, to stab”) and Komi-Permyak вундыны (vundyny, “to reap, to crop”).

Of debated origin: # From Proto-Ugric *jᴕ̈tɜ (“section, part (of body), limb; joint”). # From Proto-Finno-Ugric *jäse (“body part, joint”) (compare e.g. Finnish jäsen), though the development *s > z would be irregular.
